## Highlights

- Experimental native Windows Sandbox uses Microsoft eXecution Container (MXC) for restricted Sessions, PowerShell commands, and file operations.
- Windows launch policies support explicit broad disk reads with writes confined to granted workspaces and private temporary state. Strict read policies remain available.

## Upgrade notes

Use the co-versioned `a13n-envd-client` 0.4.0 with daemon 0.4.0. Harness 0.14.0 and Harness UI 0.14.0 require the Envd 0.4 compatibility line. Upgrade explicit executable overrides and custom endpoints alongside their clients.

Windows Sandbox requires a supported native MXC/PSEC host. Unsupported preparation fails without elevation, ACL mutation, or automatic fallback. WSL continues to use Linux execution.

## Known issues

- Broad disk reads include account-accessible Host configuration and disk credentials. This policy confines writes; it is not a Host-file confidentiality boundary. Native deny rules protect Envd bootstrap configuration, transport credentials, and broker runtime state.
- Node.js 24.21 `fs.realpathSync.native` can return `EPERM` under MXC. PowerShell, Git, and Python were exercised on the native acceptance host; validate other toolchains on the target Windows build.
